long_biography.plain_text:
Seattle selected Ken Griffey Jr. first overall from high school, and he reached the majors at 19. His fluid left-handed swing came with power and elite center-field defense. Across 22 seasons, he became the face of the Mariners, earned ten consecutive Gold Gloves and won the American League's Most Valuable Player award.

Griffey finished with 630 home runs and entered Cooperstown with the highest vote percentage the writers had yet awarded. His Seattle standing now extends into ownership: he purchased a Mariners partnership interest and, with his family, joined the Sounders ownership group. As a Mariners partner, he contributes a player's perspective to decisions about roster fit, free agency and clubhouse relationships.
